strengths: The paper addresses an important and timely problem: learning single-cell population dynamics from snapshot data while also attempting to recover interpretable gene-level interactions.

The proposed Cell-MNN architecture is conceptually appealing: a state-conditioned locally linear latent ODE gives a closed-form transition via the matrix exponential and avoids numerical ODE solvers and OT preprocessing.

The empirical interpolation results are promising. Cell-MNN achieves the best reported average EMD across the three benchmark datasets and compares against several strong recent baselines, including OT-CFM, OT-MFM, and DeepRUOT.

The paper includes useful additional experiments beyond the main benchmark, including amortized training across datasets and a scalability experiment intended to test the advantage of avoiding dataset-wide OT preprocessing.
The writing is generally clear, the method is easy to follow, and the authors provide many implementation details, hyperparameters, seeds, hardware, and appendices, which improves reproducibility.
weaknesses: The biological interpretability claim is much stronger than the evidence supports. Gene interactions are inferred by projecting a 5D PCA-space operator back to gene space, yielding a very low-rank dense interaction matrix; it is unclear whether these weights correspond to meaningful regulatory effects rather than PCA artifacts or correlations.

The TRRUST validation is limited and potentially selection-biased. Evaluation is restricted to a small set of high-activity source genes with enough TRRUST overlap, with as few as 10-65 interactions per gene, and there is no comparison to dedicated GRN inference methods, simple correlation/regression baselines, or randomized PCA/operator controls.

The gene interaction task only evaluates the sign of known TRRUST edges and does not assess edge discovery, ranking quality, calibration, false positives over non-edges, cell-type specificity, or causal regulatory validity. This weakens the claim of discovering gene regulatory interactions.

The scalability experiment is not fully convincing. The inflated datasets are generated by resampling and adding Gaussian noise in PCA space, and evaluation switches from EMD to MMD using the same type of metric used for training. OOM on a single 11GB GPU does not by itself establish broad scalability superiority over approximate or optimized OT baselines.

The amortization experiment is narrow: it uses only Cite and Multi, includes a dataset index, and merges datasets in PCA space despite different gene sets. This gives limited evidence for the broader foundation-model or transfer-learning motivation.

Some technical choices need more scrutiny. The representation f(z,t)=A(z,t)z assumes f(0,t)=0 and omits an affine term; it is not clear this holds after PCA preprocessing or for single-cell dynamics. The eigendecomposition parameterization restricts operators to real diagonalizable forms and the determinant regularizer 1/(det(P)+eps) seems numerically questionable, especially if det(P) is negative or near -eps.

The main interpolation table mixes results from prior work and rerun results, and the standard deviations are over held-out time points rather than independent training seeds for most entries. This makes statistical comparison and significance of the reported gains difficult to assess.

Ablations are limited. The paper does not isolate the contributions of local linearization, eigendecomposition, kinetic regularization, PCA dimension, MMD kernel choice, or closed-form solving versus a standard MLP transition model trained with the same loss.

strengths: The paper targets an important problem: learning single-cell dynamics from destructive snapshot measurements while also attempting to expose interpretable gene-level mechanisms.

The proposed model is simple and computationally attractive: a PCA latent space, state-conditioned locally linear ODE, analytic matrix-exponential rollout, and MMD training avoid expensive dataset-wide OT preprocessing.
The empirical section covers several relevant dimensions: interpolation accuracy, amortized training, scalability, and a preliminary biological validation against TRRUST.
The method appears to obtain competitive EMD results on the three reported single-cell interpolation datasets, with particularly strong numbers on EB and Multi.
The paper is mostly readable and includes useful implementation details such as architecture, hyperparameters, hardware, seeds, and an ethics statement.
weaknesses: The central interpretability claim is not well supported. Projecting a 5-dimensional PCA latent linear operator back to the full gene space yields a very low-rank matrix whose entries depend strongly on the PCA basis and preprocessing; treating these entries as explicit gene regulatory interactions is biologically and mathematically under-justified.

The local linear ODE formulation is close to a reparameterization rather than a substantive mechanistic discovery result. The proof that f(z,t)=A(z,t)z under f(0,t)=0 does not establish identifiability, biological causality, or that the learned A corresponds to real mechanisms from snapshot marginals.

Learning dynamics from marginal distributions alone is highly non-identifiable, but this issue is not adequately addressed. Many velocity fields can match the same observed marginals, so stronger evidence is needed before claiming discovered interactions or mechanistic dynamics.

The TRRUST validation is weak. It evaluates only a small, prediction-selected set of source genes with enough TRRUST overlap, lacks comparisons to dedicated GRN inference baselines, does not clearly handle class imbalance or statistical significance, and uses sign agreement with curated interactions as a limited proxy for regulatory discovery.

The scalability experiment is not very convincing. Inflating datasets by resampling and adding Gaussian noise in PCA space is artificial, and claiming superiority because full OT methods OOM on an 11GB GPU does not fairly compare against scalable OT approximations or optimized implementations.

The amortization experiment is narrow: it uses only Cite and Multi, merges different gene sets in PCA space, and compares against a limited set of baselines. It does not demonstrate meaningful transfer or foundation-model behavior.

Evaluation methodology is inconsistent across experiments: EMD is used for interpolation, while the scaling experiment switches to MMD, which is also the training objective. This makes the scaling claims less comparable and potentially favorable to the proposed method.

The paper claims state-of-the-art average performance, but the gains are modest and based on only three datasets with three seeds. Some baselines are copied from prior work while others are rerun, raising concerns about comparability of preprocessing, tuning, and evaluation protocols.

Several important ablations are missing, including sensitivity to PCA dimension, kernel choice, kinetic regularization, eigen-decomposition parameterization, determinant regularizer, and comparison to a generic MLP velocity model trained with the same MMD objective.

The biological claims are overstated relative to the evidence. The method may produce useful hypotheses, but the paper repeatedly frames the learned quantities as biologically consistent, interpretable gene interactions without sufficient validation or causal support.

Reproducibility is incomplete: hyperparameters are listed, but the manuscript does not clearly provide code, processed data splits, baseline configurations, or exact procedures needed to reproduce all rerun baselines and TRRUST analyses.

Overall, while the idea is plausible and some results are encouraging, the paper falls short of top-tier acceptance due to weak support for the main mechanistic/interpretability claims, limited and partially unfair evaluation, and insufficient attention to identifiability and biological validation.

strengths: The paper addresses an important and timely problem: learning single-cell dynamics from snapshot data while also extracting interpretable gene interaction structure.

The proposed Cell-MNN architecture is conceptually clean: it combines PCA compression, a state/time-conditioned locally linear ODE, and an analytical matrix-exponential decoder, avoiding numerical ODE solvers and OT preprocessing.
Empirical results are competitive on standard single-cell interpolation benchmarks, with best average EMD across the three reported datasets and particularly strong results on EB and Multi.

The scalability motivation is compelling: avoiding full-dataset Sinkhorn preprocessing is practically valuable, and the inflated-dataset experiment provides useful evidence that the method remains trainable where full OT baselines run out of memory.
The paper goes beyond predictive interpolation by attempting biological validation of learned interactions against TRRUST, which is a meaningful and relevant interpretability evaluation.
The presentation is mostly clear, with useful discussion of architecture, optimization, hyperparameters, limitations, and ethics.
weaknesses: The biological interpretability claims are stronger than the evidence fully supports. The learned interaction matrix is induced after a 5D PCA bottleneck and projection back to gene space, so individual gene-gene weights may be hard to interpret as genuine regulatory effects rather than artifacts of the low-rank representation.

The gene interaction evaluation is limited: it only evaluates a small selected subset of source genes, does not compare against dedicated GRN inference baselines, and uses sign classification against TRRUST rather than ranking or recovering edges more broadly.

The method learns from marginal distributions, so the dynamics and interactions are not identifiable without strong assumptions. The paper acknowledges snapshot limitations but does not sufficiently analyze non-identifiability or distinguish predictive consistency from mechanistic validity.

The scalability experiment relies on synthetically inflated datasets generated by resampling plus noise, and changes the evaluation metric from EMD to MMD, which is also the training loss. This weakens the strength of the scalability/performance conclusion.

The amortization experiment is promising but narrow: it covers only two datasets, still uses dataset-specific PCA embeddings merged in latent space, and does not demonstrate transfer to unseen datasets or materially different biological settings.

Some technical details deserve more scrutiny, such as the eigen-decomposition parameterization, invertibility regularizer, stability of matrix exponentials, and how complex eigenvalues or ill-conditioned eigenvectors are handled in practice.

The paper would be stronger with more ablations: latent dimensionality, PCA vs learned encoder, kinetic regularization, eigenvalue constraints, MMD kernel choices, and runtime/memory comparisons against baselines under matched settings.

Reproducibility is partial: hyperparameters and hardware are given, but the review text does not make clear whether code, preprocessing scripts, trained models, and exact baseline reruns will be released.
